text:
mike-sales: FuturePay wants to run a Private deployment POC. Their security team lists three blockers: must retain original client TCP source IP for audit logs; their inline TLS inspector needs to see original SNI; they want a fixed pair of egress IPs to whitelist. Also asked whether we can do mutual TLS from our connector to their proxy (they'll supply certs). Can netops/eng recommend one topology and paste a minimal firewall allowlist they can apply?

olan-netops: TL;DR: two recommended patterns. Option 1 = PrivateLink (interface endpoint) -> our connector in their VPC -> egress via our managed NAT/EIP pool. Fastest to provision and easiest to provide stable egress IPs. Downside: connector NATs, so at TCP level their collector will see our EIP unless you arrange customer NAT downstream. For HTTP we set X-Forwarded-For. Option 2 = VPC Peering or TGW -> route through customer's NAT/EIP (customer-controlled). More ramp on their side (route tables, TGW attachments), but preserves original TCP source IP for their audit tooling.

olan-netops: TLS inspection detail: if they require the inspector to see SNI, choose TCP passthrough (no TLS termination on our side). If we terminate TLS (to provide things like function transforms, moderation hooks, or structured parsing), SNI will be consumed by our proxy and not forwarded. Termination + header injection (X-Forwarded-Host/X-Forwarded-For) only helps app-layer logging, not TLS-layer inspection.

mike-sales: They insist SNI must be visible to their inline box. Compliance also insists original client IP must appear in logs where possible. They asked if X-Forwarded-For is enough — they seemed split.

tess-eng: Quick connector behavior notes: - For TCP passthrough we do not touch TLS bytes; downstream sees client SNI and TCP source IP (provided there is no NAT upstream of the inspector). - For proxied/terminated HTTPS we add X-Forwarded-For and can present client certs upstream (mTLS) if configured with customer certs. - We can provision a small per-customer EIP pool on request for POCs so they can whitelist known IPs.

jena-support: Pricing note: static EIP allocation is an add-on for Private deployments. For POCs we can provide up to 3 trial EIPs free for 10 days. Production EIP mapping carries a one-time setup fee + monthly management. I will prepare an SOW example once you confirm region and exact EIP count.

olan-netops: Minimal firewall snippet they can paste (replace the placeholders with our provided EIP(s) or connector CIDR depending on topology):
```
# If we egress via our managed EIPs (PrivateLink path)
ALLOW tcp 443 from 54.33.101.11/32
ALLOW tcp 443 from 54.33.101.12/32
# Allow ephemeral responses from connector subnets (health/handshake)
ALLOW tcp 1024-65535 from 10.60.0.0/24

# If using peering/TGW and customer NAT, allow connector CIDR instead
ALLOW tcp 443 from 10.50.0.0/22
```
Note: replace IPs with the actual EIP(s) we supply for the sandbox.

mike-sales: They also want a concrete test plan to validate the POC tomorrow: verify SNI pass-through, verify client-src-ip in audit logs, and validate mTLS.

tess-eng: Quick POC test plan: 1) We spin up sandbox connector and reserve 2 test EIPs (if PrivateLink path). 2) They add allowlist entries for those EIPs or the connector CIDR. 3) Test A (passthrough): TLS client -> our connector (passthrough) -> their inspector. They confirm inspector sees original SNI and client TCP src IP. 4) Test B (termination): TLS client -> our connector (terminate + proxy) -> their backend. Confirm backend receives X-Forwarded-For header with original client IP. 5) Optional mTLS: customer provides client cert + CA; we configure connector to present client certs to upstream.

deploy-bot: privatedeploy/futurepay-sandbox created id c-abc123. Console: https://deploys.redwood.example/c-abc123 :white_check_mark:

mike-sales: Perfect. Please DM the sandbox EIP list + one-page diagram I can share with their netsec before the test. I'll confirm whether they prefer PrivateLink with our EIPs or peering into their NAT.
